raw_response:
**My thinking:**

I've been farming this land in Quzhou my whole life. My father farmed it, and I know this flat North China Plain soil well. There's really only one system that makes sense here: winter wheat followed by summer maize, the same rotation everyone around me does. The land is flat, the groundwater is still reachable, and the markets for both crops are reliable — there's a procurement station nearby. I'm not going to experiment at 50. I have about 8 mu, and I'll double-crop all of it.

For wheat, I'll use Aikang 58 — I've grown it for years, it handles drought stress reasonably well and lodging isn't a problem. I'll do rotary tillage after maize harvest in October before sowing. I'll irrigate three times: once before winter freeze, once at jointing, once at heading. Four times feels like wasting water and my well isn't as deep as it used to be. I'll apply a compound base fertilizer at sowing and topdress urea at jointing. Spray herbicide early, then a fungicide-insecticide mix near heading for aphids and rust — two applications total.

For maize, I'll go with Zhengdan 958. It's proven, seed dealers always have it, and it performs consistently. I'll plant directly into the wheat stubble — no tillage, just seeding machine. Maize season gets rain so I'll only irrigate once if July is dry. One pesticide pass for corn borer and fall armyworm if needed.
